alt: A living room at dusk with the lamps lit and all four EARF pieces in Poison, a deep green acrylic: a pair of Tropos speakers with near-black cabinets and deep green stepped horns, their covers off, each on a stepped plinth that lights the floor beneath it, either side of a low oak credenza with a Mantle record player whose dark deck floats on steel posts over a thin line of warm light; a glowing green Core lamp on a side table at the left; a glowing green Hemisphere pendant over a cognac leather chair at the right; a plain plaster wall behind
notes: Each piece takes its name from the Earth. Tropos is Greek for a turn; the troposphere, the layer of air we live in, is named for it. Core, Mantle and Hemisphere are the planet’s own parts. Here all four share one room at dusk with the lights on, in Poison, one of the eight colors, at the darker stock tint the line now uses: Tropos’s thick cabinet reads near-black and its horn deep green. It is a render, not a photograph: Tropos with its stepped horn and its cover off, on its lit plinth; Core cordless; Mantle as Strata Float, its deck floating on steel posts over a strip of warm light; Hemisphere with its color outside. A daytime version of the same room exists.

header.title: Four pieces, named for the Earth.
